newsitem.title: FRANCE: EP urges EU to focus on renewables, not nukes.
newsitem.headline: EP urges EU to focus on renewables, not nukes.

text.p: The European Union needs an energy policy which gives priority to "sustainable and environmentally acceptable development", the European Parliament said on Friday.

Euro-MPs welcomed European Commission proposals for coordinating EU member states' national energy strategies -- which will be examined by EU energy ministers on May 26 -- but said draft decision COM(96)431 placed too much emphasis on creating a single EU energy market and not enough on environmental protection.
On Thursday, the parliament adopted changes which strengthened a Commission communication on the development of renewables technology -- COM(96)576 -- which is also on the Energy Council agenda.

And Euro-MPs threw out a controversial report by French Christian Democrat Andre Soulier which said nuclear energy was irreplaceable and contributed to environmental protection because, unlike fossil fuels, it did not produce CO2 emissions.

"Nuclear technology is not...appropriate...because the potential risk is too high, the problem of the disposal of the waste produced has not been solved and the cost-effectiveness ratio is poor," the parliament said in its report on common EU energy objectives.
The report, drafted by German Socialist Ulrich Stockmann, said EU spending on research should in future concentrate on improving energy efficiency and developing renewable energy sources.
The EU should only fund nuclear reaseach if it was designed to make waste storage safer, Euro-MPs said.

They also insisted, in a report on a proposed EU strategy for energy cooperation with Asia, COM(96)308, that these principles should govern the EU's energy projects in Asia, where energy consumption is set to soar.

Parliament said moves towards a more sustainable, coordinated energy policy would be boosted if EU leaders included in the revised EU treaty, due for completion in June, a chapter on energy which stressed the importance of energy efficiency and conservation of energy and natural resources.
Euro-MPs also said the Commission needed to come up with more specific proposals for attaining the common energy goals agreed by the member states, as well as for promoting renewables technology.

One suggestion from Euro-MPs is for the environmental costs of producing and using coal, oil, gas and other energy sources to be reflected in their price, a move which would make renewable resources more competitive.
Another suggestion from parliament is the creation of a European Climate Agency. Measures to combat climate change will be one of main topics on the EU Energy Council agenda.
